dropped.claim: The profitability collapse from $1.8B to $165M net income (0.8% margin) in a revenue-growth year raises red flags about structural margin pressure from tariffs, labor inflation, and competitive dynamics. OEM delays in software-defined vehicle programs directly threaten the core Advanced Safety growth thesis, while elevated inventory signals demand weakness. However, strong free cash flow of $1.5B (7.5% margin), aggressive buybacks (14% share reduction), diversified customer base across all top-selling models globally, and sustained $1.1B R&D investment suggest management is investing through a cyclical trough. The April 2026 Versigent spin-off could unlock value if it separates higher-margin technology assets from mature distribution. The $178M separation costs obscure true run-rate profitability. New tariffs (10%+ from April 2025) and Mexican wage inflation (13% in 2026) add material cost headwinds. With net debt of $5.8B and equity declining from $11.5B to $9.2B over two years, balance sheet quality is deteriorating. Watch for Q1 2026 results post-separation-cost peak and clarity on segment margins, tariff impact quantification, and inventory normalization timeline before upgrading to Dig deeper.
